comment: Still worth it for me. Premium is still cheaper than buying the albums I listen to, and I've been paying since forever. Ads on Premium are still annoying though, so I get why some people are salty.

Great, price goes up and I still can't see the full discography on desktop without a workaround. The family plan is the only reason I'm still here and even that is getting harder to justify. Hope they fix this soon or I'm back to YouTube Music.

Another price hike and the features I use keep disappearing with no explanation. Crossfade and shuffle options come and go and nobody tells you why. I'm still paying because the app is convenient, but the enshittification continues.

Bump is a few bucks more but I'm keeping my subscription. Moving years of playlists somewhere else is the real cost, not the price. I'd only leave if they broke multi-device sync or search, which is what keeps me here.

Price goes up again and the recommendations are the same songs on repeat. I already pay for YouTube Premium and that includes a music player, so Spotify makes less and less sense. Jam is the only thing keeping me here, so I'm starting to move stuff over to YouTube Music.

Price going up and I still don't have the New Episodes folder back. Episodes play in reverse and my podcasts show up empty in Wrapped. I'd pay more if the podcast side worked, but I like the UI and my playlists are here so I'm not leaving yet.

Another increase on Premium and I still get three unskippable ads before every podcast. I pay a stupid amount to be told it's ad-free music only, and that's a broken promise. If they keep the podcast ads on paid plans I'm done with podcasts here.

Cool, I'm still on free and not paying $13 for it. Premium is fine if you want it, but free Spotify is ass and I'll keep using it until they paywall something else. You can get Premium way cheaper through another country anyway.

Spotify raises prices again and the artists still get pennies for their streams. I keep paying for the support angle, but every increase just goes to the money vacuum and not to the people making the music. Buying directly is the only way I know to actually pay artists.

Premium goes up and smart shuffle still plays the same 10-15 songs over and over. I already dropped it once and went back to free because free shuffled better. Not paying more for worse shuffle, I'm out again.
Duo going up is annoying but Discover Weekly still hits every Monday and the new updates have been worth the wait. Hoping the mix feature finally reaches my account before they raise it again.

Family plan is still the cheapest way to get music, podcasts and audiobooks in one place. Yeah the bump is annoying but I've said it before: worth every penny. Not switching, the Spotify Connect setup across my devices is too good.

Premium is still the best deal I spend money on. A dollar or so more a month for ad-free access to basically everything is nothing. Free users complaining about this are missing the point. Pay the artists.

The price bump doesn't move me much. I've been paying for over ten years, my library is here, and I can't go back to Apple Music. I do wish Discover Weekly would stop recycling the same top 40 though.

Another price bump and I still get region-locked lossless and AI playlists while paying the same as everyone else. For the household it's worth its weight in gold for my parents, but I'm tired of paying more for fewer features where I live.

Not even on Premium anymore since I cancelled over the AI songs, so this doesn't hit me directly. Still, raising prices on a platform that pays artists this little is pretty gross. Glad I moved my listening elsewhere.

Raising the price on a platform that's pushing AI slop into my Discover Weekly and paying artists nothing? Hard pass. I already left once and I'm not paying more until they actually crack down on fake artists.

Premium goes up and I'm still stuck with the same bug that survives reinstalls and cache clears. Support keeps sending generic steps. Paying more for something that barely works feels bad. If this doesn't get fixed soon I'm moving to YouTube Music.

Student went from 5.99 to 6.99, which hurts when you're a broke student. Full Premium at 12.99 is just a lot. I'm mostly worried about the Hulu bundle staying put and not having to re-verify again. Still a student for now.

Premium goes up again and the mix feature still closes on me every time. Lossless sounds great when it works, but the UX sucks and perks keep vanishing on my tablet. Fix the bugs before raising prices or I'm moving to Apple Music.

Premium going to 12.99 for features that should be in the free app? Ridiculous. I'm sticking to free and I'll keep using YouTube when I want full albums. Why do I have to pay for skips in the first place?

Raising prices again without lossless is a joke. Tidal has had true lossless for ages at about the same money. I stay for the recs and features, but this tips it and I'm moving my listening to Tidal when sound matters.

Price goes up again and my songs still won't play the next track. Support is useless and I've reinstalled three times. I already cancelled Premium once, and this makes me think about just dropping it for good.

I don't care about the price bump as long as 320 is fine. Lossless is mostly hype with Bluetooth anyway, nobody can hear it. Apple Music is cheaper if you really want the quality, so people who want it can go there.

Family plan going up again is rough when I'm splitting it six ways. Still the cheapest per person I've found, so I'm not leaving. Would be nice if the extra went toward lossless, since we're still locked out of stuff half the time.

Premium price hike, cool. Better make sure the new price doesn't show up after I cancel, because last time I got charged after cancelling and support sent a copy-paste reply. I'll keep my paid plan until the billing period ends and check my statement.
I don't have premium, so this doesn't touch me directly, but it's annoying that prices keep going up while playlists still play random songs on free. Is anyone else seeing the same thing? Not great.

Spotify is more expensive than Apple Music now and the recs still repeat the same songs. I've been meaning to switch for years and this is the nudge. Probably going to Apple Music next month, though I always say that.
